name: Nuremberg Airport
before:
Bavaria's second airport after Munich, only 5 km north of Nuremberg city centre, which makes it one of the shortest airport transfers in Germany. It broke its own record in 2025 with 4,508,700 passengers, ninth busiest in the country.

The route map is domestic German flying plus European city and leisure destinations, weighted heavily towards the Mediterranean, the Canary Islands, Turkey and North Africa.

The terminal is compact and pleasant: two departure halls and one arrival hall, all connected both landside and airside, with 40 check in desks and four finger docks. Departure hall 2 was built in 1992 in steel and glass by the Nuremberg architects Grabow and Hoffmann and is full of daylight. Security moved to the ground floor between the two halls in December 2015.

One practical limit. The runway is 2,700 metres and takes everything currently flying, including the 747, but the airport is not licensed for the A380.

It is owned jointly by the state of Bavaria and the city of Nuremberg, and marketed after the painter Albrecht Dürer.
after:
Bavaria's second airport after Munich, only 5 km north of Nuremberg city centre. The U2 underground runs from outside the terminal to the main station in under a quarter of an hour.

In 2025 the airport broke its own record with 4,508,700 passengers, ninth busiest in the country. Domestic flying is now little more than the link to Frankfurt. Otherwise the map is European city and leisure flying, weighted heavily towards the Mediterranean, the Canary Islands, Turkey and North Africa.

Security sits in the middle, on the ground floor between the two departure halls, and the airport makes a point of its clear layout and short walks.

It has a single runway of 2,700 metres. The state of Bavaria and the city of Nuremberg each own half of it, and it is marketed as Albrecht Dürer Airport, after the painter.

claims.note: OurAirports lists three Bavarian airports with scheduled service: Munich, Nuremberg and Memmingen. ADV's 2025 table has Munich 43,357,559 (scheduled and charter), Nuremberg 4,508,700 and Memmingen 3,698,440 in all.
